new.title: Walk the ramparts and Jardin des Remparts
new.desc: Vannes keeps long stretches of its medieval walls, anchored by the 15th-century Tour du Connétable, built to house the constable of the Duke of Brittany's armies. A French-style garden with formal flowerbeds and old wash-houses lies at the foot of the walls.
new.tip: Free and open at all hours; the flowerbeds are at their best from April to October. Tower interiors are only open on occasional guided visits.
new.q: Jardin des Remparts, Tour du Connétable, Vannes

new.title: Visit Cathédrale Saint-Pierre and Saint Vincent Ferrer
new.desc: The Gothic cathedral of Vannes stands on the site of an earlier Romanesque church and has been a monument historique since 1906. It holds the relics of the Dominican preacher Saint Vincent Ferrer, who died in Vannes in 1419, in a chapel dedicated to him.
new.tip: Entry is free. It faces La Cohue museum, so the two combine easily in one stop.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Pierre, Place Saint-Pierre, Vannes

new.title: Find Vannes et sa femme on the old house corner
new.desc: Two carved granite busts, traditionally a Vannes burgher and his wife, look down from the corner of a half-timbered house at the Place Saint-Pierre and Place Henri-IV end of rue Noé. The 16th-century house is listed as a monument historique and is the town's best-known photo stop.
new.tip: The house is private; admire it from the street, ideally in the morning when the square is quiet.
new.q: Maison de Vannes et sa femme, rue Noé, Vannes

new.title: Admire the half-timbered houses of Place Henri IV
new.desc: The east side of Place Henri-IV is lined with 16th-century timber-framed houses with overhanging upper storeys, described as the most remarkable ensemble in Vannes. The town still has around 170 half-timbered houses, the oldest from the 15th century.
new.tip: The houses are private and best seen from the street. Combine with the nearby rue Saint-Salomon and rue Noé for more carved façades.
new.q: Place Henri IV, Vannes

new.title: Stroll the Port de Vannes and La Rabine
new.desc: The harbour of Vannes, called La Rabine, sits at the head of the Gulf of Morbihan right below the old town. A tree-lined promenade of nearly 2 km, with gardens and old plane trees, continues from the quays towards the Conleau peninsula.
new.tip: The quays are open at all times and the walk from the old town takes about 15 minutes. The Rabine car park fills early on summer weekends.
new.q: Port de Vannes, Place Gambetta, Vannes

new.title: Browse the Halles des Lices covered market
new.desc: The covered market sits on the Place des Lices, a square laid out in the 14th century, and houses thirty-odd permanent stalls selling produce, meat, fish and regional specialities. The Morbihan tourist board ranks the Vannes market among the finest in France.
new.tip: Open most mornings until about 13:30 or 14:00 and closed on Mondays in low season. Weekends are lively, so arrive early.
new.q: Halles des Lices, Place des Lices, Vannes

new.title: Step into Église Saint-Patern
new.desc: This parish church is dedicated to Saint Patern, the first bishop of Vannes in the 5th century. It stands in the old Saint-Patern quarter outside the walls and is recorded as a heritage building, with modern and older stained glass.
new.tip: Usually open in daytime; the quarter's rue de la Fontaine and rue Saint-Patern make a pleasant walk.
new.q: Église Saint-Patern, Place Sainte-Catherine, Vannes

new.title: Order a galette saucisse at Crêperie du Port
new.desc: A busy crêperie near the harbour of Vannes, rated around 4.5 on Google from almost 1,800 reviews. Reviewers single out the galette with sausage, onion and mustard.
new.tip: Book ahead, as it is often full. Pair the galette with a bolée of cider.
new.q: Crêperie du Port, Port de Vannes, Vannes

new.title: Try buckwheat galettes at Crêperie Dan Ewen
new.desc: Dan Ewen is a crêperie in the historic Saint-Patern quarter of Vannes, often named among the best in town for its galettes and crêpes. It serves traditional Breton fillings with cider.
new.tip: Expect queues at weekends. Finish with a crêpe au caramel au beurre salé.
new.q: Crêperie Dan Ewen, Rue Saint-Patern, Vannes

new.title: Eat crêpes at Crêperie Les Joséphine by the walls
new.desc: A crêperie in the heart of the historic centre since 1997, a couple of steps from the ramparts. It offers classic galettes and sweet crêpes in the old town.
new.tip: A good lunch stop after the Jardin des Remparts. Try a galette complète with a bolée of cider.
new.q: Crêperie Les Joséphine, Vannes

new.title: Bite into kouign-amann at Chez François
new.desc: Chez François makes its kouign-amann on site on the Place des Lices beside the market. Gault&Millau holds it up as a reference for a faithful, well-buttered version of the Breton cake.
new.tip: Closed Mondays, open from about 10:00 to 18:00. Buy a slice, or a whole one to carry home.
new.q: Chez François, 6 Place des Lices, Vannes

new.title: Taste the kouign-amann at Maison Le Brun
new.desc: This bakery on rue Saint-Vincent, just inside the Porte Saint-Vincent, is the house whose kouign-amann made its name according to Gault&Millau. It also bakes specialty breads and pastries.
new.tip: Go early in the day for the freshest kouign-amann.
new.q: Maison Le Brun boulangerie, Rue Saint-Vincent, Vannes

new.title: Shop the Wednesday and Saturday market
new.desc: Twice a week the Place des Lices and surrounding streets host an open-air market, with the Halles des Lices open alongside. The Vannes market is promoted by Morbihan tourism as one of the most beautiful in France.
new.tip: Held on Wednesday and Saturday mornings, roughly 8:00 to 13:30. Saturday is the busiest.
new.q: Place des Lices, Vannes

new.title: Walk or swim around the Conleau peninsula
new.desc: Conleau is a wooded peninsula in the Gulf of Morbihan a few kilometres south of the old town, with a supervised beach in season and a seawater pool separated from the gulf by a dyke. The shaded loop around the peninsula takes about 1h15.
new.tip: Reach it on the Rabine promenade and cycle path from the port. The paid car park fills quickly in summer.
new.q: Plage de Conleau, Presqu'île de Conleau, Vannes

new.title: Cruise the Gulf of Morbihan from Vannes
new.desc: Vedettes du Golfe run commentated cruises on the Gulf of Morbihan, with or without a stop on Île d'Arz and Île aux Moines, plus trips up the Auray river. Longer excursions go to Houat and Hoëdic.
new.tip: Timetables vary by season, so check the operator before booking.
new.q: Vedettes du Golfe, Presqu'île de Conleau, Vannes

new.title: Follow the Au fil de la ville walking trail
new.desc: The city of Vannes publishes a walking route through the old town linking the ramparts, cathedral, half-timbered houses and the market squares. It is a self-guided way to see the medieval streets in under two hours.
new.tip: Download the free PDF from the city website; it is easy to start from the cathedral square.
new.q: Place Saint-Pierre, Vannes

new.title: Cross by boat to the Gavrinis carved cairn
new.desc: The island of Gavrinis in the Gulf of Morbihan holds a Neolithic passage cairn whose corridor stones are covered in dense engraved patterns. It is reached only by boat from Larmor-Baden and visited only with a guide.
new.tip: Boats leave from the Pen Lannic slipway, with crossings of about 10 to 15 minutes; visits run roughly April to October. Check the Morbihan department's Gavrinis page for the timetable.
new.q: Cairn de Gavrinis, Larmor-Baden

new.title: Start at the Maison des Mégalithes in Carnac
new.desc: The visitor centre of the Carnac alignments sits at the Ménec site on the Route des Alignements, where roughly 1,050 stones stand in 11 rows. It provides the reception and information for the alignments, managed by the Centre des monuments nationaux.
new.tip: A footpath around the sites is open free all year. Hours vary by season, with longer opening from April to August.
new.q: Maison des Mégalithes, Route des Alignements, Carnac

new.title: Walk the Kermario alignments and tower
new.desc: The Kermario field is about 1,200 m long and 100 m wide with around 1,029 menhirs left in 10 rows. A stone tower, the Moulin de Kermaux, gives a view over the rows from above.
new.tip: About 1.5 km east of Ménec on the D196. In winter several alignments are open for free visits.
new.q: Alignements de Kermario, Carnac

new.title: See the Grand Menhir Brisé at Locmariaquer
new.desc: The Locmariaquer site brings together the Grand Menhir Brisé, broken into four pieces and once about 20 m tall, the Table des Marchands dolmen and the Er Grah tumulus. It is run by the Centre des monuments nationaux.
new.tip: Entry is charged, around 6 euros. Allow about an hour and a half.
new.q: Site des mégalithes de Locmariaquer, Route de Kerlogonan, Locmariaquer

new.title: Wander Sauzon harbour on Belle-Île
new.desc: Sauzon is a small harbour village on the north-east of Belle-Île, once a sardine port, with white houses and coloured shutters rising up a ria. A fortified house nearby, bought by actress Sarah Bernhardt in 1894, now holds a museum space.
new.tip: Reached by ferry to Le Palais plus bus or bike. The harbour is free to walk.
new.q: Port de Sauzon, Sauzon, Belle-Île-en-Mer

new.title: Look at the Aiguilles de Port-Coton on Belle-Île
new.desc: These jagged rock stacks on Belle-Île's wild west coast in Bangor were painted by Claude Monet, who stayed here in 1886 and made 39 canvases. The name comes from the sea foam that looks like cotton in stormy weather.
new.tip: Keep to marked paths; the site is a protected natural area on stage 2 of the GR340. Strong wind on the cliff tops.
new.q: Aiguilles de Port-Coton, Bangor, Belle-Île-en-Mer

new.title: Tour the Château de Josselin of the Rohan family
new.desc: A castle of the Rohan family above the river Oust, still lived in on its upper floors, with a formal French garden, an English-style park and a doll museum. Only the ground floor is open, freely or by guided tour that includes the first floor.
new.tip: The 2026 season ran from mid-February to early March and from early April to 1 November; check the official site for winter opening.
new.q: Château de Josselin, Place de la Congrégation, Josselin

new.title: Climb the keep of the Château de Suscinio
new.desc: A medieval castle of the Dukes of Brittany in Sarzeau on the Rhuys peninsula, with banquet hall and duchess's apartments. The tower top gives a view across the marshes, the ocean and Sarzeau.
new.tip: Guided visits last about 45 minutes; ticket office closes an hour before the castle. Summer evenings bring a light show on the walls.
new.q: Château de Suscinio, Route du Duc Jean V, Sarzeau

new.title: Explore the Cité de la Voile Éric Tabarly
new.desc: A sailing museum and interactive centre at Lorient La Base in a former submarine base, opened on 28 April 2015 in glass-and-metal architecture by Jacques Ferrier. It has hands-on exhibits, a 4D cinema, an Éric Tabarly section and sailing trips in the Lorient roadstead.
new.tip: Open daily in school holidays and summer; check citevoile-tabarly.com for the exact season.
new.q: Cité de la Voile Éric Tabarly, Rue Roland Morillot, Lorient

new.title: Board the submarine Flore at Keroman
new.desc: The Flore S645, a Daphné-class submarine 57.75 m long, served from 1964 to 1989 and is now exhibited in the Keroman 2 bunker of the former German submarine base, built 1941 to 1944. A museum precedes the guided audio visit aboard.
new.tip: The site opened in May 2010; hours and prices from older sources, so check la-flore.fr before visiting.
new.q: Sous-marin Flore, Base de sous-marins de Keroman, Rue Roland Morillot, Lorient

new.title: Visit the Citadelle de Port-Louis museums
new.desc: The citadel at Port-Louis houses the Musée de la Compagnie des Indes, with ship models, Chinese porcelain and Indian cottons, and the national Navy museum. One ticket covers both.
new.tip: Guided visits are listed for 2026; check the museum website for hours.
new.q: Citadelle de Port-Louis, Avenue du Fort de l'Aigle, Port-Louis

new.title: Wander flower-decked Rochefort-en-Terre
new.desc: A Petite Cité de Caractère and one of Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, Rochefort-en-Terre was the first town to get the Petite Cité label in 1978. The castle ruin and American painter Alfred Klots's restoration, and the collegiate church Notre-Dame-de-la-Tronchaye, are the main sights.
new.tip: Castle gardens open about May to September; the village streets are free all year.
new.q: Rochefort-en-Terre, Place des Halles

new.title: See the Grail church in Tréhorenteuc
new.desc: The Église Sainte-Onenne, called the Grail church, was restored between 1942 and 1962 by rector Henri Gillard. Its stained glass by Henri Uzureau, a mosaic of the white hart by Jean Delpech and altarpieces by Karl Rezabeck bring Arthurian themes into a village church.
new.tip: Guided visits titled Il était une foi(s) run on some mornings. It is the start point for the Val sans Retour walk.
new.q: Église de Tréhorenteuc, Tréhorenteuc

new.title: Study the Danse Macabre at Kernascléden
new.desc: Notre-Dame de Kernascléden was started in 1420 and completed in 1464 under Alain IX de Rohan. Its wall paintings, dated around 1430 to 1440 and found in 1912, include a Danse Macabre and a vision of Hell.
new.tip: Kernascléden and the chapel of Kermaria an Iskuit are the only Breton sanctuaries known for this theme.
new.q: Chapelle Notre-Dame de Kernascléden, Kernascléden

new.title: Visit the Sainte-Anne-d'Auray sanctuary and Scala Santa
new.desc: One of Brittany's great pilgrimage sites, the sanctuary has a basilica, a cloister and a Scala Santa, a holy staircase pilgrims climb on their knees. The Grand Pardon of Sainte-Anne is held each year on 26 July.
new.tip: The grounds are free to enter. Heavy crowds on pardon days.
new.q: Sanctuaire de Sainte-Anne d'Auray, Sainte-Anne-d'Auray

new.title: Walk the port of Saint-Goustan in Auray
new.desc: Saint-Goustan is the medieval river port of Auray, with a stone bridge over the river, half-timbered houses and a quay where Benjamin Franklin landed in December 1776. Rue du Petit Port alone has nine very old timber-framed buildings.
new.tip: The bridge and quays are free. Waterside restaurants line Quai Franklin.
new.q: Port de Saint-Goustan, Auray

new.title: Walk the 15th-century walls of Hennebont
new.desc: The Ville Close of Hennebont is ringed by almost intact 15th-century ramparts, with the twin Broërec towers flanking the main gate as the town's emblem. Parts of the Levée ramparts were listed in 1941 and the remains in 1947.
new.tip: Free game booklets for families are available at the town hall all year.
new.q: Porte Broërec, Ville Close, Hennebont

new.title: Climb to the Cairn de Petit Mont in Arzon
new.desc: This Neolithic cairn near Port Crouesty dates from around 4600 BC and stands 36 m above the sea, with views to Belle-Île, Houat, Hoëdic and the Gavrinis cairn. A bunker was built on the site in the Second World War.
new.tip: Open to visitors around April to September, with guided visits and workshops; check hours first.
new.q: Cairn de Petit Mont, Arzon

new.title: Buy the original caramel au beurre salé in Quiberon
new.desc: Henri Le Roux began making his salted butter caramel (CBS) in Quiberon in the 1970s; it won best sweet at the 1980 Paris confectionery show and the CBS trademark followed in 1981. The Port-Maria boutique at 18 rue de Port-Maria is the original shop.
new.tip: The caramels are now made in Landevant, so the shop is the original address only; confirm opening hours.
new.q: Maison Le Roux, 18 Rue de Port-Maria, Quiberon

new.title: Slurp oysters at Les Viviers de Loc'Ker
new.desc: A waterside tasting spot on the Kerpenhir road with views over the Gulf of Morbihan, serving oysters straight from the producer.
new.tip: Whole seafood platters must be ordered the day before.
new.q: Les Viviers de Loc'Ker, route de Kerpenhir, Locmariaquer

new.title: Taste oysters at Bar à huîtres Le Kermancy
new.desc: An oyster bar run by Mickaël Tanguy on the Pointe de Kermancy at La Trinité-sur-Mer, open for tastings all year at weekends from 10:00 to 16:00.
new.tip: In season tastings are by reservation only. Try the local huîtres de La Trinité.
new.q: Bar à huîtres le Kermancy, Pointe de Kermancy, La Trinité-sur-Mer

new.title: Taste Blanche Hermine at Brasserie Lancelot
new.desc: Brasserie Lancelot, founded in 1990 by Bernard Lancelot, is set in the renovated 19th-century buildings of the former Villeder gold mine at Roc-Saint-André. Its beers include Blanche Hermine, brewed from barley and buckwheat, and the Telenn Du, and a distillery makes whisky since 2017.
new.tip: The shop is open Monday to Friday; tasting visits need reservations.
new.q: Brasserie Lancelot, 7 La Mine, Le Roc-Saint-André, Val d'Oust

new.title: Try caramel and biscuits at La Bien Nommée
new.desc: A Belle-Île biscuit and confectionery maker in Le Palais, founded in the late 1990s by Christophe and Myriam Niceron. It bakes Breton cakes and caramel creams on the island without additives; a window overlooks caramel production.
new.tip: Shop beside the workshop and another on Place de la République; the workshop viewing is weekday mornings.
new.q: La Bien Nommée biscuiterie, Le Palais, Belle-Île-en-Mer

new.title: Eat oysters and the day's catch at Ma Mer
new.desc: A seafood restaurant at 22 Quai Franklin in the port of Saint-Goustan focused on Gulf of Morbihan oysters, the day's catch and natural wines.
new.tip: Book for dinner. Order the oysters of the gulf.
new.q: Ma Mer, 22 Quai Franklin, Auray

new.title: Order galettes at Café Breton in Rochefort-en-Terre
new.desc: A small crêperie at 8 rue du Porche with an interior and garden terraces, praised by reviewers for its galettes and crêpes and rated 4.6 on Wanderlog.
new.tip: Booking is wise, since the room is small.
new.q: Café Breton, 8 Rue du Porche, Rochefort-en-Terre

new.title: Have a crêpe at La Chaumière on Île aux Moines
new.desc: A crêperie, brasserie and saladerie with a terrace on Place du Ru Vraz in the village centre of Île aux Moines.
new.tip: Last dinner service is about 18:00 in low season and 22:00 in high season. Take the ferry from Port-Blanc in Baden.
new.q: Crêperie La Chaumière, Place du Ru Vraz, Île-aux-Moines

new.title: Taste canned tuna at Groix et Nature
new.desc: An artisanal cannery at Port-Tudy that keeps up Groix's tuna-fishing tradition, with a shop selling regional products and canned fish. Guided visits with a tasting run by reservation.
new.tip: Open daily in season. The tuna with white beans is one of the specialities.
new.q: Conserverie Groix et Nature, Port Lay, Île de Groix

new.title: Visit the Belle-Iloise sardine cannery in Quiberon
new.desc: La Belle-Iloise cans sardines, tuna and mackerel in Quiberon and offers a free visit of about 45 minutes at its historic factory in Port-Maria. The company also bought the other historic cannery, La Quiberonnaise, in late 2023.
new.tip: Reports differ on booking; confirm on labelleiloise.fr under the visit section. Buy a tin of sardines in olive oil.
new.q: La Belle-Iloise, 10 Rue de Kervozès, Quiberon

new.title: Queue for galettes at Chez Marie in Carnac
new.desc: Chez Marie at 3 Place de l'Église claims to be the oldest crêperie in Carnac, dating from 1959. It is usually full every day with a queue outside.
new.tip: No reservations in summer, so go early or off-peak.
new.q: Crêperie Chez Marie, 3 Place de l'Église, Carnac

new.title: Eat a galette at Crêperie Ar Kastell in Josselin
new.desc: A crêperie at 4 rue du Château in the historic centre of Josselin, listed open all year in 2026 when several nearby places close for winter.
new.tip: A safe off-season option near the château.
new.q: Crêperie Ar Kastell, 4 Rue du Château, Josselin

new.title: Eat fish at Le Poulpe in Lorient
new.desc: A fish restaurant and friendly bistro on Avenue de la Perrière in the port area, opened in 2010 by Rejane and Mathieu, serving the catch landed at nearby Keroman.
new.tip: Fish comes from Lorient's fishing port, France's first fish auction. Book for dinner.
new.q: Le Poulpe, Avenue de la Perrière, Lorient

new.title: Join an oyster-farm visit at Île de Seniz
new.desc: The Le Gros family farm at Kerouarch in Locmariaquer runs a guided visit of its oyster site on Thursday mornings, ending with a tasting of oysters and shrimp by the Gulf of Morbihan.
new.tip: Thursdays at 10:30; book by phone by Wednesday evening. Listed April to September 2026.
new.q: Les Huîtres de l'île de Seniz, 80 Kerouarch, Locmariaquer

new.title: Circle Île d'Arz on foot or by bike
new.desc: A coastal path of about 17 km goes all round the island of Île d'Arz in the Gulf of Morbihan. Bike rental is at the Béluré landing, and bikes are banned on the Bilhervé peninsula.
new.tip: Ferries leave Vannes and Séné in about 25 minutes. Bikes are not carried on cruises, so rent on the island.
new.q: Île d'Arz, Béluré, Golfe du Morbihan

new.title: Walk round Île de Berder at low tide
new.desc: Île de Berder at Larmor-Baden is joined to the mainland by an 80 m causeway that is only passable at low tide. The island is private but the coastal path stays open, and the walk pairs well with a Gavrinis visit.
new.tip: Read the tide notice at the crossing, as you can be stranded for hours. Mid-tide is calmer than early low tide.
new.q: Île de Berder, Larmor-Baden

new.title: Hike the Quiberon Côte Sauvage
new.desc: The wild west side of the Quiberon peninsula follows the GR34, with Port Bara beach, the Port Blanc arch and Pointe du Percho. A 16.3 km loop links Penthièvre and Quiberon with little climbing.
new.tip: Check tide times, since parts are cut off at high tide, and take care near the cliffs in wind. Start at Porz Stang.
new.q: Côte Sauvage, Port Blanc, Quiberon

new.title: Hike the Donnant dunes and Goulphar loop
new.desc: A loop of about 12 km from Bangor passes the Donnant beach and its dunes, owned by the Conservatoire du Littoral, with views of the Goulphar lighthouse. Donnant is a known surf spot.
new.tip: About three hours of walking. Bus line 2 from Le Palais serves Donnant Village.
new.q: Plage de Donnant, Bangor, Belle-Île-en-Mer

new.title: Visit Grands Sables, the convex beach of Groix
new.desc: The Grands Sables beach on Groix is one of Europe's rare convex beaches and drifts about ten metres a year. The Trou de l'Enfer, a rocky gully where the sea roars, is reachable by the coastal path.
new.tip: Take the ferry to Port-Tudy and rent a bike. Swimming is best in summer.
new.q: Plage des Grands Sables, Île de Groix

new.title: Go to the Festival Interceltique de Lorient
new.desc: A ten-day festival of Celtic music and culture in Lorient, held each August for decades. The 2026 edition ran from 31 July to 9 August, and the 2027 edition is listed for 30 July to 8 August.
new.tip: Book accommodation well ahead, and check the official programme for the year.
new.q: Festival Interceltique de Lorient, Palais des Congrès, Lorient

new.title: Walk or paddle the south shore of Lac de Guerlédan
new.desc: The south side at Saint-Aignan has a walking circuit of about 10 km along the GR341 and GR37, with the chapel of Sainte-Tréphine, and a canoe-kayak base at the Anse de Sordan.
new.tip: The full lake circuit is open from 1 March to 15 September; parts close for hunting outside that period.
new.q: Anse de Sordan, Saint-Aignan, Lac de Guerlédan

new.title: Hike the Val sans Retour in Brocéliande
new.desc: A valley near Tréhorenteuc tied to the Arthurian legend of Morgan le Fay, who shut away unfaithful knights. The walk passes the Miroir aux Fées pond and the Arbre d'Or, with a short 1.6 km loop accessible to all.
new.tip: Park in the village and take the signposted track. A longer 14.7 km loop to Trécesson takes about four hours.
new.q: Val sans Retour, Tréhorenteuc

new.title: See the Festival Photo La Gacilly
new.desc: Outdoor photography exhibitions spread through the streets of La Gacilly, free to visit. The 23rd edition ran from 1 June to 4 October 2026.
new.tip: Each year's dates are on the festival site; the shows are free.
new.q: Festival Photo La Gacilly, La Gacilly

new.title: Walk the GR34 from Port-Navalo on the Rhuys peninsula
new.desc: The coastal path from Port-Navalo leads along the mouth of the Gulf of Morbihan towards the Pointe de Bilgroix, with views over the gulf. Nearby loops link Tumiac, Port-Navalo and the Pointe de Penbert.
new.tip: The Pointe du Grand Mont is reached from Saint-Gildas-de-Rhuys, not directly along this stretch.
new.q: Port-Navalo, Arzon

new.title: Cruise the whole gulf with Vedettes l'Angélus
new.desc: Vedettes l'Angélus run a three-hour classic tour of the Gulf of Morbihan with a stop on Île aux Moines, or a 1h30 version without a stop, plus day trips to Houat and Hoëdic.
new.tip: Trips ran daily from 5 April to 30 September 2026 and over the autumn holidays; check the current timetable.
new.q: Vedettes l'Angélus, Embarcadère du Guilvin, Locmariaquer

new.title: Glide by electric boat with an oyster tasting at Baden
new.desc: L'Huître La Toulverne at Baden combines an electric-boat outing in the gulf with an oyster tasting on board. Quoted at 49 euros for adults and 29 euros for children under 12.
new.tip: Prices from the listing; booking required.
new.q: La Cabane à Huîtres, L'Huître La Toulverne, Baden

new.title: Watch the fish auction at the Keroman criée
new.desc: Lorient-Keroman is billed as the first criée and first fishing port of Brittany by tonnage and value. Guided visits with the Maison de la Mer let you watch the live computerised auctions.
new.tip: Dates and prices are listed on the tourist office site; book ahead.
new.q: Port de pêche de Keroman, boulevard Louis Nail, Lorient

new.title: Join the Grand Pardon at Sainte-Anne-d'Auray
new.desc: The annual Grand Pardon of Sainte-Anne takes place each 26 July and draws thousands of pilgrims. Pilgrims climb the Scala Santa on their knees at the sanctuary.
new.tip: Expect large crowds and plan transport early.
new.q: Sanctuaire de Sainte-Anne d'Auray, Sainte-Anne-d'Auray

new.title: See Breton draft horses at Haras National d'Hennebont
new.desc: The Hennebont stud, rooted in Napoleon's national stud network, is known for Breton draft horses and has the largest museum space of any stud in France. A national show-jumping competition takes place there every July.
new.tip: Equestrian shows are a main draw; check the programme before going.
new.q: Haras national d'Hennebont, 35 rue de la Bergerie, Hennebont
